$comment: C9 · a late registration catching up over more input than the process may hold (I-10).
Produced by: cargo test --release -p schweep-soak --test c9_memo_ceiling -- --nocapture
MACHINE-DEPENDENT: resident memory is an allocator and kernel figure, so no test recomputes
these rows, and they vary between runs on one machine — the ranges below are measured, not
estimated. The deterministic half of C9's measurements is c9-bounds.json, which IS recomputed
Three findings are recorded here rather than in a commit message, because each one changed what
1. through_a_log — streaming the history out of schweep_log::Log peaked at 342 MB, because a
Log holds every sealed batch resident. The catch-up was flat; the feeder was not.
2. one_binary_per_measurement — the gate first shared a binary with its correctness test and
failed the full-workspace run at 123.9 MB against a 96 MiB budget, having peaked at 54.6 MB
alone. Resident memory is a property of the process.
3. per_pass_residue — the catch-up's resident memory climbs monotonically, and it is per PASS
rather than per byte of state. That is why the gate asserts a coefficient and not flatness.

shape.sql: SELECT a.id AS id FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id WHERE a.id < 100

through_a_log.verdict: FAILED the gate: the feeder held the history

one_binary_per_measurement.verdict: the gate now lives in its own test binary; correctness moved to c9_late_registration.rs

replay_phase.$comment: 349 epochs into a memo with nothing registered. Its own curve, because it is its own regime.

catch_up_phase.$comment: One sample per chunk the memo pulls. Peak and growth both vary between runs; the range is over four runs on one machine.
catch_up_phase.assertion: grown bytes < 12.5% of the input streamed

through_a_stream.verdict: PASSED: peak resident memory is a sixth of the input it streamed and a twenty-second of the state it built

$comment: Three probes, same query, isolating whether the monotone climb is per pass or per byte of state.
It is per pass: many small chunks climb, few large chunks carrying the same total data do not.
Whether the residue is retained allocator arenas or redb's per-commit bookkeeping is NOT
established. It bounds how long a history a single catch-up can cross, and it is filed for C10.

compared: the late registration (registered at epoch 30, caught up from the stream)
a registration present from epoch 0, stepped epoch by epoch
the oracle, recomputed from scratch over the same history
correctness.verdict: all three agree, byte for byte (I-1)
